topics.name: Air India 787 Dreamliner Crash
topics.summary: Boeing 787 crashed on takeoff in Ahmedabad, India with 242 passengers and approximately 1-2 survivors. Delian Asparouhov theorized flaps-up takeoff as likely cause and argued cockpit communication failures are a systemic aviation safety issue untreated by the FAA. Boeing stock fell 5%.

topics.name: YC Demo Day 2025
topics.summary: Hosts attended YC Demo Day noting 90% AI focus, mostly B2B agent infrastructure. Gary Tan reported 45% of YC companies reach Series A with $1M+ median ARR. Compared to Teal Fellowship which focuses on deep tech like bio and BCI with decade-long timelines.

topics.name: Stripe Acquiring Privy
topics.summary: Stripe acquired Privy, a crypto embedded wallet company, following its earlier Bridge acquisition. Both deals involved Sequoia and Paradigm. Patrick Collison framed it as enabling a new generation of global internet-native financial services.

topics.name: Meta Acquiring Scale AI
topics.summary: Meta acquiring ~49% of Scale AI for $14-15B; Alex Wang to join Meta; Jason Droege named new CEO. Competitors see opportunity to win displaced customers. Bill Gurley questioned why creative deal structures persist despite Lena Khan's departure.

topics.name: CS Graduate Unemployment vs Art History Majors
topics.summary: NY Fed data shows CS grads at 6.1% unemployment vs 3% for art history, but sample sizes are 108K vs 2K graduates. Hosts concluded the spike is a lagging indicator of big tech hiring freezes post-2022, not AI displacement—though AI is a partial contributing factor.

topics.name: End of Software / AI Coding
topics.summary: Chris Paik argued LLMs commoditize code writing making creativity and agency the scarce resource. Proposed that word cells won over shape rotators. Hiring now means candidates must ship a working piece of software on the same day.

topics.name: Aviation Safety and Pilot Training
topics.summary: Delian argued cockpit communication failures cause most crashes and that the FAA ignores this by not mandating role-playing simulation training. Systemic fraying attributed to COVID pilot retirements, 1970s ATC software, and Boeing's cost-cutting culture.

topics.name: Stablecoins and Crypto Fintech
topics.summary: Stablecoins seen as first crypto technology giving incumbents like Airbnb and Uber reason to adopt crypto rails for treasury efficiency and global payouts. Circle IPO performed well. Privy acquisition by Stripe seen as accelerating this trend.

topics.name: Apple WWDC / iOS 26
topics.summary: iOS 26 praised for fluid Liquid Glass UI; iPad OS 26 seen as productivity breakthrough for most computing tasks. MLX on-device inference framework may unlock a viral AI Flappy Bird moment. Anthropic Xcode partnership underreported.

topics.name: Stargate Data Center Project
topics.summary: Bloomberg reporter confirmed Abilene Texas site is real and expansive; SoftBank financing project-by-project; 10 more US sites planned. OpenAI diversifying hyperscaler relationships beyond Microsoft to Oracle and SoftBank.

topics.name: Dodd-Frank 1033 Open Banking Rule
topics.summary: CFPB under second Trump administration may undermine open banking rule in ways that go beyond reversing Rohit Chopra's overreach, potentially allowing banks to cut off data access to crypto and competitive fintechs. Zachary Perret expressed concern about foreclosing consumer choice.

topics.name: E-bikes and Micro Mobility Second Era
topics.summary: Infinite Machine launched Alto e-bike at $3,495 as owned vehicle versus first-era sharing economy model. Joseph Cohen argued ownership creates emotional connection like cars. Tariffs have stabilized but US industrial policy still lacks incentives for domestic re-industrialization.

topics.name: AI Fraud and Financial Security
topics.summary: Plaid launched Protect anti-fraud product using cross-network data including impossible travel detection and account age signals. Financial fraud rising ~25% annually, often AI-driven or government-sponsored from Southeast Asia. Static SSNs are insufficient fraud detection.

topics.name: Top-Down vs Bottom-Up Companies
topics.summary: Chris Paik proposed framework: top-down companies (Apple, Tesla, SpaceX) hire innovators and ship multiple flagship products. Bottom-up companies (Google, Facebook, Reddit) capture lightning in a bottle once and can only grow additional products via M&A.

topics.name: Future of Work in the AI Age
topics.summary: Sam Altman's blog post and Chris Paik argued history shows productivity booms create new leisure-based jobs; modern sports invented with Industrial Revolution. Omakase chefs and athletes cited as human roles that cannot be replaced by AI due to human narcissism in leisure.

topics.name: Elon Musk and Donald Trump Reconciliation
topics.summary: Reports indicate Musk and Trump spoke privately and are back to being friends after public fallout; Teddy Schleifer at NYT described as being on full-time Elon beat waiting for the next blowup.

topics.name: NYC Mayoral Race
topics.summary: Zoran Mamdani surging to 42% on Polymarket vs Andrew Cuomo's declining numbers; Mamdani's rent freeze and police reduction proposals noted; described as a textbook example of narrative discipline by Signal analyst.

topics.name: Networking Infrastructure Market
topics.summary: Meter raised $170M arguing that networking is the oldest and largest part of technology but almost no new companies get started in it; vertically integrated networking-as-a-service model disrupting 1990s-era legacy vendors.
